newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger, helped by dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger, helped by dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Thursday, helped by gains in the Canadian dollar and recent U.S. economic data suggesting growth there may be slowing, analysts said.

"This morning the initial (U.S.) jobless claims were a little bit on the high side," said Michael Gregory, fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers. "The data is suggesting that things are indeed slowing down. That's continuing to provide a little bit of spark here."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.35 to C$110.15 to yield 7.136 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.95 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 21 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets were stronger in the wake of a U.S. report out this morning that showed initial U.S. jobless claims for the week ended April 26 rose to 347,000. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast initial claims of 325,000.
Analysts said Canadian bonds also benefitted from strength in the currency, which firmed past C$1.3940 (US$0.7174) in early trade.
Weaker U.S. data has taken a lot of pressure off the Canadian dollar, which had weakened on concerns that a U.S. rate hike was imminent, said Gregory.
In new issue news, the Bank of Canada tomorrow at 1530/1930 will release details of the federal government's auction of 10-year bonds on May 7.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds rose C$0.19 to C$102.77 to yield 6.604 percent. The U.S. bond rose 3/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 11 basis points from nine basis points on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.12 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.22 percent.
